commands.review_summary:
The PR makes sandbox stat classify missing paths through a reserved stdout marker instead of English stderr matching and adds mocked regression coverage.

PR surface: Source +22, Tests +70. Total +92 across 3 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: create a dangling symlink under an anchored sandbox path and call bridge stat; the proposed `test -e` branch emits the missing marker before GNU stat can report the symlink entry. The original locale bug is also source-reproducible, although no live localized-container run was supplied.

target.title: fix(sandbox): missing stat paths use locale-independent marker
target.body:
Closes #105187

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running sandbox containers with a non-English locale would get a thrown `stat failed` error for a missing file instead of the bridge returning `null` when the container's `stat` diagnostics are localized.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper's preferred fix is a structured, locale-independent missing-path result from the stat command plan—not English stderr matching and not `LC_ALL=C` alone. The plan now checks for basename existence with `[ ! -e "$2" ]`, prints a reserved marker, and the bridge maps only that marker to `null`. Permission and other nonzero failures still throw. Linked open PR #105263 explores `LC_ALL=C`; this follows the issue review's best-solution shape instead.

**Fix quality:** compatibility — one canonical missing-path path, no dual English-stderr shim; performance — one extra existence check before `stat` only on the bridge path; usability — missing files stay null across locales; security — path-safety checks and non-missing failures unchanged.

## User Impact

Sandbox-backed file checks return the expected missing-file (`null`) result regardless of container locale. Permission and other filesystem failures remain visible errors.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.anchored-ops.test.ts src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.shell.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  20 passed (20)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard

$ pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.ts src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge-shell-command-plans.ts src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.anchored-ops.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ git diff --check
(clean)
```

New coverage:
- plan script includes existence check + `SANDBOX_STAT_MISSING_MARKER`
- missing path returns `null` when stdout is the marker even if French-style stderr is present
- non-missing failures (permission denied) still throw

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: sandbox `stat` of a missing path returns `null` without depending on English `No such file or directory` stderr.
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout at HEAD after this patch; focused Vitest with docker-exec mocks (agent-solo unit-or-source).
- Current-main contrast: `fs-bridge.ts` only treated missing files when stderr included the English phrase `No such file or directory`, so localized containers threw instead of returning null.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.anchored-ops.test.ts src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.shell.test.ts`
  2. New test injects French-style missing-file stderr plus the reserved marker and expects `null`.
  3. Control test injects permission-denied stderr + nonzero code and expects throw.
- Evidence after fix: 20/20 focused tests pass; missing-marker case resolves to `null`; permission case rejects with `/permission denied/i`.
- Control check: only the missing-marker path returns null; permission/other failures still error; existing anchored stat size/path tests still pass.
- Observed result after fix: missing paths are classified by the plan marker, not locale-specific diagnostics.
- What was not tested: live non-English Docker container end-to-end; host-backend (non-docker) path uses the same plan when shell is used.

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Human operator did not manually write the patch; proof is the focused Vitest transcript above.
